title: Change approval and authorization
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Production changes are deployed only through one pipeline from reviewed, approved commits; the pipeline generates a change record linking work item, commits, author and approvers, check results, artifact digest and deployment; sponsors receive a per-release notice of changed control-relevant modules; change records are retained as service-organization evidence.
current_practice: No production environment or deployment pipeline exists. Echelon tool repositories use Praxis work items and CI validation for their own releases.
intended_practice: Production changes are deployed only through one pipeline from reviewed, approved commits; the pipeline generates a change record linking work item, commits, author and approvers, check results, artifact digest and deployment; sponsors receive a per-release notice of changed control-relevant modules; change records are retained as service-organization evidence.
provable: Nothing for a production service; no Echelon production system exists as of 2026-11-25.
customer_statement: Echelon intends to implement this as part of Unbound's initial build; it is not in operation today and no evidence is available yet.

title: Segregation of duties in development and deployment
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: The pipeline enforces that no identity, human or agent, can author, approve and deploy the same change; control-relevant modules need two approvers other than the author; repository and pipeline administrative changes are themselves reviewed and alerted; exceptions are recorded with approver and expiry. Where headcount is insufficient for independent human approval, Echelon will disclose this and use an external reviewer rather than claim segregation it does not have.
current_practice: Not established. Echelon's organizational headcount is not established in reviewed records; Limen's CODEOWNERS names one owner account for guardrail paths.
intended_practice: The pipeline enforces that no identity, human or agent, can author, approve and deploy the same change; control-relevant modules need two approvers other than the author; repository and pipeline administrative changes are themselves reviewed and alerted; exceptions are recorded with approver and expiry. Where headcount is insufficient for independent human approval, Echelon will disclose this and use an external reviewer rather than claim segregation it does not have.
provable: Nothing for a production service; no Echelon production system exists as of 2026-11-25.
customer_statement: Echelon intends to implement this as part of Unbound's initial build; it is not in operation today and no evidence is available yet.
open_questions: How many independent humans with production-relevant authority will Echelon have at launch?

challenge.customer_intent: Prevent fraud or sabotage by a single insider and catch mistakes.
challenge.adverse_outcome: One person deploys a malicious or erroneous change to money-moving code.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Effective where real independence exists; in very small companies it is often nominal.
challenge.legally_required: Not by statute for Echelon; SOX 404 applies to public-company customers' own controls and flows down through their reliance on SOC reports.
challenge.contractually_required: Expected by SOC 2 auditors (CC8.1) and bank vendor reviews.
challenge.historical_convention: Separate developers, approvers and operations staff.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Cannot be eliminated by architecture; it is about people. Automation can enforce that rules are followed but not create independent people.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Automated enforcement plus provenance plus external reviewer for control-relevant changes when internal independence is absent.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes from pipeline and source control records.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Uncertain for a founder-led company with AI agents doing most work.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: A single administrator able to alter branch protection or pipeline rules without detection.
challenge.alternative_risks: Agents counted as independent approvers would make segregation illusory.
opposing_arguments: AI agents are not independent humans; counting them would be misleading.
Small-company reality may not meet customer expectations.

title: Deployment, rollback and database migration safety
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Application releases are immutable artifacts that can be rolled back; database changes are deployed only as Strata plans that are compiled, diffed and judged for breaking effects, with destructive steps blocked by default; schema changes follow expand-and-contract so application rollback remains possible; rollback and restore are tested before release; after any restore, money movement stays blocked until reconciliation (CNV-ARC-001).
current_practice: Strata exists as a pilot schema tool that judges what each change would break before applying it (strata@c6a384ec); it is not operated for a production Echelon database.
intended_practice: Application releases are immutable artifacts that can be rolled back; database changes are deployed only as Strata plans that are compiled, diffed and judged for breaking effects, with destructive steps blocked by default; schema changes follow expand-and-contract so application rollback remains possible; rollback and restore are tested before release; after any restore, money movement stays blocked until reconciliation (CNV-ARC-001).
provable: Nothing for a production service; no Echelon production system exists as of 2026-11-25.

title: Change evidence and infrastructure as code
status_rationale: Praxis work protocol and provenance exist and are used for Echelon repositories; integration with a deployment pipeline, signing and infrastructure as code for a production service do not exist.
target_answer: Infrastructure and database schema are declared as code and deployed only from declarations, with daily drift detection. Change evidence is generated by construction: Praxis records the work item, actor (human or agent with model and runtime) and content digests; the pipeline adds approvals, artifact digests and deployment records; records are signed and retained under the service-organization evidence class. Echelon distinguishes self-reported actor identity from authenticated identity and binds the two through the source control platform's authenticated accounts.
current_practice: Praxis (praxis@12bf9951) records work transitions, actor identity and content digests as append-only events in Echelon repositories. No production infrastructure or deployment pipeline exists.
intended_practice: Infrastructure and database schema are declared as code and deployed only from declarations, with daily drift detection. Change evidence is generated by construction: Praxis records the work item, actor (human or agent with model and runtime) and content digests; the pipeline adds approvals, artifact digests and deployment records; records are signed and retained under the service-organization evidence class. Echelon distinguishes self-reported actor identity from authenticated identity and binds the two through the source control platform's authenticated accounts.
provable: Praxis event logs and provenance in Echelon tool repositories; first-party, not independently verified, not for a production service.
customer_statement: Echelon's repositories record each work item and its human or AI contributor through its Praxis tooling. Production change evidence and infrastructure as code are planned with the first production service.

challenge.customer_intent: Be able to verify that changes were controlled, without relying on the vendor's word.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Unauthorized change goes undetected because change records are incomplete or editable.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Ticketing systems and change advisory boards produce manual records that are often incomplete and reconstructed for audits.
challenge.legally_required: No; SOC 2 CC8.1 and customer audits require evidence.
challenge.contractually_required: Common for SOC 2 and bank customers.
challenge.historical_convention: Change tickets with CAB approval, sampled by auditors.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Manual record keeping is eliminated if records are produced by the only path to production.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Pipeline is the only path to production; Praxis validation fails on unattributed changes.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Evidence by construction from work protocol, source control and pipeline.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes if records are signed and the pipeline is the only path; auditors can test completeness by comparing deployments to records.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely; auditors increasingly accept system-generated change evidence.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Any deployment path outside the pipeline; Praxis actor fields accepted without binding to authenticated accounts; editable event logs.
challenge.conventional_cost: Manual ticket overhead and audit preparation.
challenge.alternative_risks: Praxis actor identity is self-reported by the executing process; on its own it is attribution, not authentication or approval.
supporting_arguments: Records cannot be forgotten if they are produced by the only path.
opposing_arguments: Praxis is not an approval system and does not authenticate actors.
Auditors must still test the pipeline's completeness.
